entries.title: test:record with no file argument silently skips every test/slow fixture
entries.summary: node scripts/run-tests.mjs record defaults its node --test target to test/*.test.mjs, so regenerating a bd recording for a test/slow scenario requires naming the file explicitly or the command succeeds while changing nothing.

entries.title: scaledTimeout() is inert under apra-fleet-se npm test, because only run-tests.mjs exports the concurrency var
entries.summary: test/helpers/scaled-timeout.mjs reads APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY, which is set only by scripts/run-tests.mjs; the package.json test script passes --test-concurrency=8 without it, so every scaledTimeout caller runs on its unscaled base budget under the suite that actually has contention.

entries.title: serve-wiring-integration.test.mjs times out under full npm test concurrency but passes in isolation
entries.summary: test/serve-wiring-integration.test.mjs spawns a real bin/serve.mjs subprocess and waits for its dashboard to render; under the full `npm test` run (test-concurrency=8, ~700 files), its 'GET / returns 200' and outer describe both timed out around 90-92s, but running the file alone passed in 3.7s -- a resource-contention flake, not a functional regression.

entries.title: The only real-timer watchdog test lives in test/slow and is not run by npm test, so a withDispatchWatchdog change can regress unnoticed
entries.summary: dispatch-watchdog.test.mjs uses node:test mock timers and cannot catch an unref'd-timer regression; the test that can, test/slow/dispatch-watchdog-timer-ref.test.mjs, is excluded from the default suite by the package.json glob.

entries.title: A dispatch-pin falsification edit must reuse an existing anchor, or siteFor fails first and masks the real check
entries.summary: siteFor() asserts exactly one matching agent() site before any pin-level comparison runs, so falsifying a pin-collision assertion with an invented anchor string turns the subtest red for the wrong reason and looks confirmed.

entries.title: install --force must stop the registered service, not pkill: launchd/systemd relaunch under a new pid
entries.summary: killApraFleet() signals apra-fleet by process name, which cannot stop a supervised server; the fix is ServiceManager.stop() (graceful exit 0) first, with pid-delta detection to tell a relaunch from a process refusing to die.

entries.title: Editing an agents/schemas/*.json contract forces two generated-artifact updates
entries.summary: A role-contract schema change is never a single-file edit: the schema is inlined into auto-sprint.js by a build-time generator with a drift guard, and it is embedded verbatim in the happy-path golden transcript's dispatch prompt.

entries.title: Replacing a content[0] text reader with resultText also closes a false-success in provisionOutcome
entries.summary: provisionOutcome's non-structured fallback tests the extracted text for a leading [FAIL]; an unfiltered content[0] read returns the display banner instead, so a failed provision classified as success.

entries.title: ConcurrentSyncBracketError is thrown from a finally block, so it masks the dispatch error it races
entries.summary: A crossing sync-bracket close throws from inside withOpenSyncBracket's finally, replacing any in-flight exception from the bracketed dispatch, so the original failure is lost from the log exactly when it is needed.

entries.title: dispatchRole has 12 call sites for 13 role-policy-table entries by design
entries.summary: doer-resume shares role-policies.mjs's policy object with doer via ROLE_POLICIES['doer-resume'] === ROLE_POLICIES.doer.secondary, and is dispatched from doer's own call site rather than a distinct one, so an inventory of dispatchRole call sites will correctly find 12, not 13, against 13 named roles.

entries.title: The checked-in .beads/issues.jsonl export is stale and must not be used to answer bead-state questions
entries.summary: issues.jsonl in this repo is a passive export last committed 2026-08-18 and contains none of the current sprint's beads, so grepping it for bead state yields silently wrong answers.

entries.title: Only scripts/run-tests.mjs makes scaledTimeout() non-inert in the apra-fleet-se suite
entries.summary: scaledTimeout() scales only when APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY is set, and scripts/run-tests.mjs is the single writer -- any raw node --test invocation silently runs every scaled budget unscaled.

entries.title: Provider abstraction: six adapters, never assume Claude
entries.summary: src/providers/index.ts registers exactly six LlmProvider adapters -- claude, codex, copilot, agy, opencode, none -- matching the LlmProvider union at src/types.ts:4. There is no gemini adapter. Any auth, credential or dispatch change must route through the ProviderAdapter interface rather than assuming Claude-specific fields, and getProvider() defaults to claude only when the argument is null/undefined.

entries.title: OK_REASONS classifies skipped_local_member as ok:true, so callers must check reason before the generic ok/fail branch
entries.summary: src/tools/provision-auth.ts's OK_REASONS array includes 'skipped_local_member' alongside 'ok'/'deployed_unverified'/'deployed_with_errors', so structuredContent.ok is TRUE for a local-member skip. Any consumer branching on structuredContent.ok alone will misclassify a skip as a genuine successful provision.

entries.title: Same-slug callers now open two SqliteProvider handles on one kb.sqlite
entries.summary: Keying the KB provider cache by (slug, repoPath) means two local clones of the same remote get two separate SqliteProvider instances pointed at the same kb.sqlite file; this is safe by design because init sets WAL plus busy_timeout=5000.

entries.title: A missing-anchor freshness regression surfaces first as kb_list dropping entries, not as a stale-flag assertion
entries.summary: In tests/knowledge/kb-remote-member-e2e.test.ts the four remote-member assertions live in one it(), so removing SqliteProvider's anchorIsMissing guard fails at the SAME DATABASE read-back (line 165) and never reaches the raw stale-row check (line 181).

entries.title: runSprintCycle's sync-bracket extraction needs TWO construction points, not one
entries.summary: openSyncBracketCount is declared at the top of runSprintCycle before command/doltPushMutex/agent exist, so createSyncBrackets must be called there and createGitSync only later, where withGitSync used to be defined.

entries.title: bd-replay drift is one-directional, so a regenerated fixture may legitimately shrink
entries.summary: Replay only errors when an issued command has no remaining recorded response; recorded entries that are never consumed are silently ignored, so a refreshed recording with fewer entries than the one it replaces is not evidence of lost coverage.

entries.title: KB provider cache is now keyed by (slug, repoPath), not slug alone
entries.summary: getKbProviders/_providers Map keys on providerKey(slug, repoPath) via a NUL join, so two callers resolving to the same project slug but different repoPath values get distinct provider instances, each anchored at its own caller's repoPath.

entries.title: A guard module added to GUARDED_MODULES must never write 'agent(' or 'command(' inside a backtick template literal on a non-comment line
entries.summary: dispatch-safety-guard.mjs's findCallSites() same-line-string filter (isInsideSameLineString) tracks only single/double quotes, deliberately not backticks, so a template-literal string containing the literal substring 'agent(' or 'command(' on a non-comment line is misdetected as a real call site once that file is itself registered in GUARDED_MODULES.

entries.title: Streak id survives on the beads even though the lane grouping drops it from its return contract
entries.summary: groupStreaksFromLaneMetadata discards the lane id from its return value, but every bead in the returned arrays still carries metadata.streak, so streak identity is recoverable per-bead on that one path.

entries.title: A vcs_token or secure.NAME placeholder survives single quotes but breaks inside double quotes
entries.summary: Both placeholder substitutions inject an ALREADY-quoted value, so a placeholder inside the caller's single quotes still composes correctly by POSIX quote-concatenation, while the same placeholder inside double quotes leaks literal quote characters into the argument and causes a false 401.

entries.title: Only the execution dispatch-pin file guards against anchor collision
entries.summary: execution-role-dispatch-pins.test.mjs asserts its 14 pins resolve to 14 distinct sites; the planning file has no equivalent check over its 8, so a future anchor collision there would silently leave a dispatch unpinned.

entries.title: bin/cli.mjs self-invokes main() under `node --test`, breaking phase4-moveonly-probe.mjs whenever cli.mjs enters the Phase-4 diff-intersection
entries.summary: phase4-moveonly-probe.mjs runs `node --test <file>` on both BASE and CURRENT revisions of every file in its diff-intersection; bin/cli.mjs's isMainModule() guard treats that invocation as a direct CLI run (process.argv[1] equals the probed file), so main() executes for real and exits 1 on missing required flags on both revisions, classifying UNEXPLAINED and failing the gate.

entries.title: secure.NAME token values arrive already shell-escaped, and the escaping is OS-branched
entries.summary: execute_command replaces each secure.NAME token with a value that has ALREADY been quoted for the target member's shell -- escapePowerShellArg for windows members, escapeShellArg otherwise, chosen from agentOs. Reference the token bare in a command string; wrapping it in your own quotes double-escapes the value and surfaces as a false 401 or invalid-token error. This entry deliberately writes the token without its surrounding double braces: kb_session_prime injects KB entries verbatim into every agent dispatch prompt, and execute_prompt rejects any prompt matching the braced secure-token pattern, so spelling it in full here makes every dispatch in a sprint fail.

entries.title: A bd replay fixture can encode a FAILED bd init and still make its scenario pass
entries.summary: apra-fleet-mock-sprint-liar.jsonl was recorded from a run whose `bd init` exited non-zero with truncated stdout; replay served that failure back forever and no test noticed until the harness started checking init's exit status.

entries.title: The 3-bead golden guard's false-stall signature is [3,3,3]/high-water-4, not the single-bead [1,1,1]/high-water-2
entries.summary: Mutating away the 66u.4 close loop in build3BeadFleetApi() does fire a real StalledSprintError, but with a different arithmetic shape than the single-bead file, so pattern-matching on [1,1,1] will miss the 3-bead regression.

entries.title: Watchdog label literals are not always inside the agent() call, so they are unsafe pin anchors
entries.summary: A runner.js label: literal may live in withDispatchWatchdog's options rather than the agent() options object, in which case it matches zero AGENT_SITES and cannot anchor a dispatch pin.

entries.title: Driving all 22 dispatches generically requires resolving a dispatch's owner by object identity, secondary-first
entries.summary: doer-resume is both a table key and the identical frozen object at ROLE_POLICIES.doer.secondary, so a main-first identity lookup tries to drive it by name and fails; scanning for a secondary owner first is what makes a whole-table census possible without a hand-written role map.

entries.title: A node --test child spawned via execFileSync inside another node --test run silently no-ops unless NODE_TEST_CONTEXT is stripped
entries.summary: node --test sets NODE_TEST_CONTEXT=child-v8 in its own process env (even standalone, not just nested). A node --test <files> child spawned via execFileSync while that var is inherited returns empty stdout and exit 0 in well under a second instead of actually running the requested files -- a false pass that looks identical to a genuine fast-passing run unless you check elapsed time or the TAP pass/fail counts.

entries.title: bd prints literal JSON null, not [], for an empty dolt remote list
entries.summary: `bd dolt remote list --json` emits the JSON literal null when no Dolt remotes are configured. parseDoltRemoteList maps that to [] before its non-array guard, so an unwired repo reads as "no remotes" rather than a parse error; every other non-array shape still throws. Without the null branch, checkDoltRemoteAbsent returns ok:false ("could not parse") for a repo that is simply not wired to a Dolt remote.

entries.title: GUARDED_MODULES literal-['runner.js']-baseline KB entry is stale; guard tests derive dynamically
entries.summary: A KB entry claims four guard test files deepStrictEqual GUARDED_MODULES against a hardcoded ['runner.js'] array, but on the current tree GUARDED_MODULES already lists 9+ non-runner modules and every guard test (dispatch-safety-guard, dolt-literal-guard, guarded-modules-coverage, full-db-fetch-tripwire, pause-guard-push-holes) asserts against guardedModuleBasenames()/GUARDED_MODULES read dynamically, not a literal array.

entries.title: A nested `node --test` child inside the apra-fleet-se suite must cap its own --test-concurrency
entries.summary: package.json runs the suite at --test-concurrency=8, so any test file that spawns a nested node --test child at the same concurrency doubles peak parallelism and makes wall-clock-budget tests in unrelated files fail intermittently.

entries.title: Migrating a ladder onto dispatchRole reddens a predictable set of runner.js-only source censuses, several of which must be RETIRED rather than count-bumped
entries.summary: Six guard files hard-count agent() sites or withGitSync brackets in runner.js. The first migrations only need the counts lowered; the last ones drive the counts to zero and the census must be re-anchored onto the policy table plus a real engine run.

entries.title: A behaviour change invalidates a bd replay fixture even when the test text is untouched
entries.summary: bd recordings pin the exact bd command sequence a scenario issues, so changing runner.js behaviour (not the test) makes an already-recorded fixture replay the OLD world and fail confusingly; re-record with the same single-file record command.

entries.title: Local members use host OAuth; provision_llm_auth skips them
entries.summary: Local fleet members share the orchestrator's own machine, so they use whatever OAuth session is already active on that host. provision_llm_auth explicitly skips local members rather than attempting to provision credentials for them.

entries.title: The wiring test must strip APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY from the child env or it self-masks
entries.summary: Because the wiring test runs inside npm test, the var is already in its own env; without an explicit delete the nested child inherits it and a regressed test script passes green.

entries.title: A throw from a mocked execute_command is degraded, not propagated, under failSoft
entries.summary: WorkflowEngine._commandDispatch converts a transport-level rejection into { ok: false, error: <message> } when opts.failSoft is set, so a fail-closed throw inside the mock-sprint harness surfaces as a soft failure message rather than unwinding the sprint.

entries.title: A vitest mock returning the wrong SHAPE hides inside a best-effort try/catch and still reports green
entries.summary: tests/cloud-lifecycle-unit.test.ts stubbed provisionAuth with a bare string while lifecycle.ts read result.structuredContent.ok; the TypeError was swallowed by reProvisionAuth's best-effort catch, so 9 tests passed while every real call failed. Assert on the absence of the warning log, not just on resolves.toBeDefined().

entries.title: The VCS stderr pattern-table census no longer covers the file that owns the classifier
entries.summary: vcs-nongithub-auth-selfheal.test.mjs scans only runner.js for a re-declared GIT_/DOLT_ pattern table, but classifyGitFailure now lives in git-topology.mjs, which nothing scans.

entries.title: sprint-logs/ must never carry a blanket directory ignore -- .gitignore says so inline
entries.summary: A directory-level rule such as '/sprint-logs/' shadows everything beneath it, un-ignore patterns included, and silently breaks the sprint cost ledger because auto-sprint.js stages it with an unguarded `git add sprint-logs/`. Merged main keeps only scoped rules and records the prohibition as a comment in .gitignore itself, so the lesson survives without depending on the KB.

entries.title: kb-setup is the one kb tool that takes repo_path but resolves no KB
entries.summary: Fifteen of the sixteen src/tools/kb-*.ts tools spread kbScopeFields and forward repo_remote_url to getKbProviders; kb-setup is excluded by design because its repo_path only locates a .git dir for hook installation and it writes a single global config, never selecting a project KB.

entries.title: All four kb_ sites now log symmetric rejected and failed lines via isToolError
entries.summary: Supersedes the earlier claim that kb_query was silently swallowing isError results; the only remaining silent case is an unparseable non-error payload.

entries.title: The mock vcs_credential_exec reports a failed dispatch as ok, unlike the real tool
entries.summary: The harness simulator does not wrap its delegate executeCommand call, so the two failure shapes that mock fleet api can produce -- an isError spawn failure and a thrown unmocked-network guard -- do not map to the real tool's dispatch_failed reason.

entries.title: shell-command-guard misses shell expansions inside multi-line template literals
entries.summary: segmentLine() in fleet-sprint/shell-command-guard.mjs classifies quoting context one line at a time, so any $VAR, ~/ or $( ) sitting on a continuation line of a multi-line template literal is treated as plain code and never reported.

entries.title: The supervisor's dolt-orphan-sweep arms on a 5-minute interval with no immediate first pass
entries.summary: createDoltOrphanSweep().start() only arms a setInterval(DEFAULT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 5 min) and never runs sweepOnce() eagerly, so a supervisor process that lives under 5 minutes never sweeps at all -- the basis for any time-bounded mitigation of its machine-wide kill scope.

entries.title: Retiring the orchestrator-side credential read breaks 5 test files, two of them positionally
entries.summary: Routing raiseVcsPrForMember's create-PR dispatch through vcs_credential_exec removes one commandLog entry, which breaks two files that INDEX the log tail by offset in addition to the three that filter it by content.

entries.title: A nested `node --test` child silently no-ops unless NODE_TEST_CONTEXT is stripped from its env
entries.summary: Spawning `node --test` (directly or via scripts/run-tests.mjs) from inside a test that is itself already running under node:test inherits NODE_TEST_CONTEXT=child-v8 by default, which makes node's test runner treat the nested invocation as recursive and skip running any files -- it exits 0 with zero tests and no output, which looks like success unless the caller checks for expected side effects.

entries.title: Root npm test is now about 7 minutes end to end, not 8-12, and backgrounding it works fine
entries.summary: Measured on this branch: vitest 312.7s (321 files, 4537 tests) then the apra-fleet-se node --test suite 99.0s (3418 tests), around 7 minutes total, contradicting the older 8-12 minute vitest-alone estimate.

entries.title: Routing the PR-raise through vcs_credential_exec drops it out of the workflow journal and activity log
entries.summary: raiseVcsPrForMember's create-PR dispatch moved from the workflow engine's command() path to a raw callTool, so it no longer emits activity events, is no longer journaled/replayable, and loses its dispatch label.

entries.title: sandbox-lock.mjs has no read-only ownership query, so ordering around release is load-bearing
entries.summary: authorizeAndReleaseLock both authorizes and unlinks in one call, and the CLI exposes only acquire/mark-server-started/release -- so any Teardown step placed BEFORE the release runs unconditionally, including against a sandbox owned by a different live run.

entries.title: plan-reviewer findings: empty array means plan-wide, absent means pre-contract
entries.summary: The new optional findings field distinguishes an empty array (explicit plan-wide objection) from an absent field (verdict predates the contract), which is what lets the contested-bead consumer migrate off prose scanning without changing behaviour.

entries.title: A sprint-state hoist test must assert constructions AND resolutions, because creating the state alone keeps the construction count at 1
entries.summary: Counting only 'at most one fleet client construction per sprint' passes vacuously when resolveSettleShell is reverted to per-call construction, because createSprintState still builds and logs its own client; the resolution-count half is what actually catches a bypass.

entries.title: Only two runner.js role ladders use a bounded attempt loop; the rest express retry as nested try/catch
entries.summary: Grepping for an attempt-counter loop in runner.js finds exactly reviewer and plan-reviewer, so any guard that detects retry depth by loop bound silently misses the other eleven roles.

entries.title: All fleet-sprint ladders are migrated, so both dispatch-pin tables' inline halves are empty and no anchor search runs
entries.summary: PLANNING_LADDERS/EXECUTION_LADDERS contain zero mode:'inline' entries, so planning-role-dispatch-pins.test.mjs pins nothing textually and renaming a ladderAnchor at a real dispatch site does not fail it. The role-policies.mjs ladderAnchor-shadowing hazard is latent, not live.

entries.title: A regionBetween() anchor pair silently widens when the END anchor moves into a later module of the concatenated scan set
entries.summary: execution-role-dispatch-pins builds SRC by concatenating DISPATCH_LADDER_MODULES in order, so moving an end anchor into a phases/* module stretches a one-line region across every module in between -- and the test stays GREEN while measuring almost nothing.

entries.title: apra-fleet-se npm test fails on Node < 21 due to node --test glob non-expansion
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-se `npm test` (node scripts/run-tests.mjs mock) exits 1 with 'Could not find test/*.test.mjs' under Node 20 because node --test does not expand globs before v21; run with a shell-expanded file list to actually execute the suite.

entries.title: Usage-limit pause/resume is inert: detectUsageLimit has no runtime caller
entries.summary: On fleet-sprint/hzeb-usage-limit-pause, the provider detectUsageLimit methods and the fleet-sprint pause/resume controller both exist but are never connected: execute_prompt never calls detectUsageLimit and nothing sets details.reason==='usage_limit', so the whole feature never triggers at runtime.

entries.title: The mock-sprint harness epic stays open at P2, making not-vacuously-strict assertions vacuous
entries.summary: Any mock-sprint assertion of the form 'some final bead is open with priority <= goal' is satisfied by the harness's own scenario epic, which is never closed, so it proves nothing about the bead under test.

entries.title: The mock-sprint harness's default member_detail carries no os field, so every mock sprint exercises the uncached OS degrade
entries.summary: defaultMockCallTool answers member_detail with only vcsProvider, so resolveMemberTarget always throws internally, degrades to { os: 'linux', shell: '' } and never caches -- meaning member_detail is re-dispatched on every settle-shell resolution in mock sprints.

entries.title: objectLiteralFor's brace walk was comment-blind, so extractions near FIXED_ROLE_TIER silently broke model-tier pins
entries.summary: test/helpers/dispatch-pin-scanner.mjs's objectLiteralFor skipped string literals but not comments, so an apostrophe in a comment opened a phantom string and desynced the walk; it was green only by luck until a runner.js extraction flipped it to null.

entries.title: beads-scope wrapCommand only invalidates on a command that RETURNS, not one that throws
entries.summary: The written invalidation contract says every beads-mutating command through the wrapper drops the snapshot, but the wrapper awaits rawCommand first with no try/finally, so a throwing mutation leaves a stale snapshot.

entries.title: hasOppositePolarity matches on word-boundary regexes, not substrings
entries.summary: audn.ts hasOppositePolarity tests NEGATIVE_PATTERNS/POSITIVE_PATTERNS with precompiled word-boundary regexes, so "prefixed" no longer collides with "fixed".

entries.title: A single unpaired apostrophe in an objectLiteralFor comment is enough to swallow the real closing brace via later string quotes
entries.summary: Reverting objectLiteralFor's comment-skip branches turns one stray apostrophe in a `//` or `/* */` comment into a phantom string-open; skipStringLiteral then chains through every subsequent quote character in the file (each closing quote is misread as a new opening quote), consuming the literal's real closing brace along the way and returning null instead of a truncated string.

entries.title: role-policies-table.test.mjs proves retry budgets via four declared shapes, superseding the earlier gap entry
entries.summary: Every role's retry.attempts and retry.resumeAttempts is now re-derived from runner.js through a per-role ROLE_SOURCE.attempts shape, so the earlier entry claiming these two fields were unproven is obsolete.

entries.title: apra-fleet-se's plain npm test never sets APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-se's "test" script runs node --test directly with --test-concurrency=8, but does NOT set the APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY env var -- only the separate test:unit/test:integration/test:record scripts (which route through scripts/run-tests.mjs) set it. A scaledTimeout()/waitFor() call that relies on the env var being set will silently use an unscaled timeout under plain npm test.

entries.title: raiseVcsPrForMember degrades every auth failure, including pre-PR provisioning, instead of throwing
entries.summary: As of the 5co8.15 fix, raiseVcsPrForMember catches a provisionPrCapableAuthForMember failure and returns authFailure:true rather than throwing, so both callers (Publish PR and finalizeAbort) skip the PR and let the sprint keep its computed verdict.

entries.title: runner.js makes exactly 22 agent() dispatches, partitioned 8 planning and 14 execution
entries.summary: Eleven role ladders each have a main dispatch and a max_turns-exhaustion resume; the two dispatch-pin test files cover all 22 with no overlap and none unpinned.

entries.title: Measured runtime of the apra-fleet root npm test, both suites, September 2026
entries.summary: npm test runs vitest then the apra-fleet-se suite unconditionally; measured 300.6s and 135.9s respectively, correcting an older KB estimate of 8-12 minutes for vitest alone.

entries.title: inline-ladder-guard no longer skips an unresolvable member kind silently -- it throws, so the two older KB entries saying otherwise are stale
entries.summary: After apra-fleet-3swo.66, memberExprFor() resolves pool-head and runtime bindings and findInlineLadderViolations() throws for any dispatch with a member it cannot resolve, so entries describing a silent skip no longer describe the tree.

entries.title: Extracting a fleet-sprint module out of runner.js breaks dispatch-safety-guard's EXPECTED_COMMAND_COUNT
entries.summary: test/dispatch-safety-guard.test.mjs hard-asserts the number of command()/agent() call sites in runner.js, so any move-only extraction that carries a command() call site out of runner.js fails that test even though every site stays compliant.

entries.title: runner.js's re-export of fatal-diagnostics.mjs is load-bearing for abort.mjs, not just compatibility sugar
entries.summary: abort.mjs imports findDoltDivergedCause back out of the runner.js facade, so deleting the facade re-export as dead code would break isTypedAbortError and the BEADS_SYNC_CONFLICT terminal state.

entries.title: The inline vcs_token escaper omits the CRT-argv layer that fleet-sprint's PowerShell shQuote applies
entries.summary: escapePowerShellArgInner only doubles single quotes, while fleet-sprint's shQuote also backslash-escapes embedded double quotes for the native CRT parser, so the two halves of a PowerShell create-PR command are escaped by different rules.

entries.title: Streaks are anonymous bead arrays by the time they reach the doer dispatch, so the sync bracket deliberately carries no streak identity
entries.summary: groupStreaksFromLaneMetadata discards metadata.streak after grouping, selectStreaks never has a lane id, and harvester has no streak -- so streak identity is unavailable on 2 of 3 pushCode:true paths, and there is no per-streak branch to key exclusivity on.

entries.title: The phase4 gate now decides anchor-desync by experiment, superseding the wording rule
entries.summary: classifyFailure only decides FACADE_BREAK; corroborateAnchorDesync re-runs the file's current committed revision to split ANCHOR_DESYNC from UNEXPLAINED, so assertion wording no longer decides and the gate is PASS again.

entries.title: The engine-derived retry.attempts check in role-policies-table is self-referential
entries.summary: role-policies-table.test.mjs feeds the engine retry.attempts+1 failures and then asserts the engine made retry.attempts dispatches, so mutating the shipped value cannot fail that file; the execution pin file is what guards the value.

entries.title: runner.js dispatch options must be read spread-base-first, inline-last, or a pin reads a value the engine never uses
entries.summary: Every role dispatch repeats member_name inline after spreading its shared opts object, so the inline key -- not the base object -- decides the effective value; a mutation to the base object alone is a no-op.

entries.title: The regression playbook 18300-series port claim came from a test-only base port, not a product constant
entries.summary: regression-test-playbook.md's old '18300-series fleet-sprint dashboard ports' rationale traces to packages/apra-fleet-se/test/spawner.test.mjs:629, which picks a random base port in 18300-18499 for test isolation. No product constant defines an 183xx range.

entries.title: Node's process.platform is win32 under Git Bash even though the invoking shell is POSIX-like
entries.summary: A Node script invoked from Git Bash on Windows sees process.platform === 'win32' (native node.exe), so platform-detection in a helper script should branch on process.platform, never on which shell/tools (lsof, pgrep) happen to be on PATH -- that lets a script correctly pick the Windows-native probe (netstat/taskkill, Get-CimInstance) even when run from a POSIX-shaped shell.

entries.title: Falsify a phases/* slice by set-diffing against the pre-commit runner.js in both directions
entries.summary: Extract the regions from `git show HEAD:<runner.js>` rather than the diff's minus-lines, normalise whitespace and sort, then run comm both ways: one direction proves nothing was dropped, the other proves nothing but scaffolding was added.

entries.title: A crossing sync-bracket close can never be the last open bracket, so the pause-guard poke is unreachable there
entries.summary: withOpenSyncBracket's CROSSING-close branch is entered only while another bracket sharing the key is still open, so openSyncBracketCount is always >= 1 after the decrement and the count===0 pause-guard poke cannot fire on that path.

entries.title: guarded-modules.mjs's GUARDED_MODULES baseline is hard-asserted to ['runner.js'] by four tests
entries.summary: Adding a newly extracted fleet-sprint module (e.g. mcp-result.mjs) to GUARDED_MODULES breaks dispatch-safety-guard.test.mjs, dolt-literal-guard.test.mjs, and guarded-modules-coverage.test.mjs, which deepStrictEqual the shared list against the literal array ['runner.js'] in multiple 'today' baseline assertions.

entries.title: A facade re-export test must use namespace imports, or a dropped export fails as a SyntaxError
entries.summary: A test that asserts runner.js still re-exports moved symbols must read them off a namespace import; a static named import turns a dropped re-export into a module-load SyntaxError that kills the file before any assertion runs.

entries.title: kill-port.mjs owns the playbook's bounded-retry port-guard semantics, so playbook guards are one-liners
entries.summary: Every regression-playbook port guard (18700, 18701, 3001) is a single kill-port.mjs invocation; the 5s bounded retry, re-kill-each-pass, probe-tool hard-fail and fail-loud exit all live in waitPortFree(), not in the playbook's shell.

entries.title: vcs-auth.mjs's facade pin fails on ADDED top-level symbols, not just removed ones
entries.summary: vcs-auth-extraction-facade.test.mjs asserts its two MOVED_*_SYMBOLS lists and vcs-auth.mjs's top-level declarations agree symbol-for-symbol, so introducing a new top-level helper turns the gate red exactly like deleting one does.

entries.title: abort.mjs still classifies pre-sprint refusals by message prefix, which is why their wording is load-bearing
entries.summary: isTypedAbortError's last branch matches err.message.startsWith('Pre-sprint validation failed:'), so the four refusal messages in runSprintCycle are a behavioural contract even now that they are raised as a typed PreSprintValidationError.

entries.title: Check a fleet-sprint extraction facade against the pre-move commit export surface
entries.summary: Grep the parent commit's runner.js for exported symbols in the moved region to prove the re-export list is complete, rather than eyeballing the new module's exports.

entries.title: resolveGitProviderForClassification must gain an export keyword in any git-topology slice
entries.summary: It is module-private in runner.js but is called by the syncMember* brackets that stay behind, so extracting the classifier layer forces it across the module boundary even though runner.js must not re-export it.

entries.title: The .trim() guard in resolveProjectSlug is provably redundant and cannot be pinned by any test
entries.summary: project-slug.ts guards its remote-URL short-circuit twice, but the outer remoteUrl.trim() check is unreachable-by-effect given slugify, so no input can distinguish its removal and no regression test can pin it.

entries.title: A verbatim extraction out of runner.js breaks textual test anchors in unrelated test files, and the re-anchor has two halves
entries.summary: Tests that assert against a raw fs.readFileSync of runner.js desync on a move-only extraction even though the code is byte-identical; re-pointing the assertion is only half the fix, the now-dead source read and its comments must go too.

entries.title: apra-fleet-5co8.40's closed status does not reflect its acceptance criteria being met
entries.summary: Bead apra-fleet-5co8.40 (curl/wget basename matching for absolute-path invocations) is marked closed, but CURL_WGET_TOKEN_RE in mock-sprint-harness.mjs is still an exact-match regex with zero test cases for path-prefixed curl/wget invocations -- the described fix was never implemented despite the close.

entries.title: dispatchReview has exactly two consumers, Review and Re-Review, not three
entries.summary: Final Review does not receive dispatchReview -- it only cites it in a boilerplate comment that six other phase modules also carry, so a grep for the identifier across phases/ badly overcounts its real consumers.

entries.title: The KB scope selector is kbScope(remoteUrl), not scopeOf(repoPath) as bead texts claim
entries.summary: Planning documents describe a repoPath-keyed scopeOf helper, but the real helper keys on the git remote URL and emits repo_remote_url alongside a separately passed repo_path.

entries.title: provision_llm_auth and provision_vcs_auth ok flags reproduce the old cross-mark prefix test exactly
entries.summary: The OK_REASONS and VCS_OK_REASONS allowlists were chosen so structuredContent.ok is true for precisely the outcomes whose prose did not start with the failure emoji, which is why the logLine and preflight-cache side effects did not shift when the emoji were retired.

entries.title: Balanced-paren scans of runner.js must mask comments first or call ranges run away to EOF
entries.summary: runner.js prose comments contain apostrophes, which a string-skipping paren scanner reads as an opening quote; it then swallows real code including closing parens, so a call site's balanced range silently extends to end-of-file.

entries.title: A migrated role's ladderAnchor deliberately matches ZERO agent() sites, so the inline-ladder guard's zero must be falsified per role
entries.summary: Once a role is marked migrated the anchor assertion inverts: matching no call site is the expected state, which means checkModules()'s zero says nothing on its own and has to be proven falsifiable by seeding a ladder for every role migratedRoleNames() returns.

entries.title: shell-command-guard false-positives on nested templates and on any dollar-word in prose strings
entries.summary: The guard flags constructs in ANY JS string, not just member-bound command strings, and segmentLine() mis-tracks nested template literals -- so registering existing fleet-sprint siblings in GUARDED_MODULES fails on non-violations today.

entries.title: Moving a phase body into a module loses in-flight reassignments on the throw path, and runSprintCycle is what makes that safe
entries.summary: A phase module that reassigns params and returns them keeps success-path semantics exactly, but drops partial assignments if it throws mid-phase; that is unobservable only because no try/catch sits between the phase call sites and the Cycle Evaluation reads.

entries.title: kill-port netstat parsing depends on the colon-anchored port suffix
entries.summary: parseNetstatPids matches the local address with endsWith(':<port>'); the leading colon is what stops port 3001 from also matching netstat rows for 13001/23001/53001.

entries.title: toolErrorText survives a contentless isError envelope, so the kb_ rejected-logging paths cannot throw
entries.summary: A degenerate MCP result of exactly {isError:true} with no content array still produces a usable log line ('no error text returned') instead of throwing inside the non-fatal handler.

entries.title: dolt-sync-brackets.test.mjs blows the suite's own 5-minute per-file budget via real backoff sleeps
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-se/test/dolt-sync-brackets.test.mjs runs about 6 minutes because retry-exhaustion tests use the real default sleep with 8 retries capped at 30s, not injected fake timers.

entries.title: runner.js sometimes stacks JSDoc blocks in reverse order, detached from their function several hundred lines away
entries.summary: Before apra-fleet-3swo.6.11, the JSDoc comments for kbPromotionBlock and kbKnowledgeBlock physically preceded KB_SELF_INJECTING_ROLES's own doc and definition, while the actual kbPromotionBlock/kbKnowledgeBlock function bodies sat 60-100 lines further down with no doc immediately above them. A doc block ending right before another doc block (no code in between) is the tell that it belongs to a function defined later, not the next declaration.

entries.title: The smoke test's supervisor uptime bound is enforced in Test scenario step 4, not in Teardown
entries.summary: Teardown's SUPERVISOR_UPTIME >= 300 check only prints a warning; the actual enforcement of the dolt-orphan-sweep mitigation is step 4's UPTIME_DEADLINE = SUPERVISOR_STARTED_AT + 280 hard-stop, so any regression test must assert on the 280s branch.

entries.title: role-policies-table.test.mjs deployer retry-ladder subtest fails on feat/runner-refactor-standalone tip
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-se/test/role-policies-table.test.mjs:602 'deployer: attempts, backoff, resume escalation...' fails at derivedAttempts (line 257) with 'runner.js re-dispatches this ladder after a failure', making npm test exit 1 on the branch tip independent of any provisioning work.

entries.title: The phase4 move-only gate is red from the watchdog commit, not from any contract change
entries.summary: phase4-move-only-completeness.test.mjs reports planning-role-dispatch-pins.test.mjs as UNEXPLAINED; bisection shows commit 99e0ece0 introduced it, and the pre-sprint baseline plus the intervening structured-response commit both pass.

entries.title: renderDegradeNote throws on a missing template, so degrade.classes and degrade.noteTemplates must move together
entries.summary: Adding an error class to a row without adding its note template turns a survivable degrade into an uncaught throw out of dispatchRole; the only thing preventing it is one test.

entries.title: Extracting finalizeAbort/appendRejectedFindingToParentNotes out of runner.js also breaks vcs-capabilities-table.test.mjs's vcsCapabilities() call-site count, not just dispatch-safety-guard
entries.summary: Beyond the already-documented dispatch-safety-guard.test.mjs EXPECTED_COMMAND_COUNT breakage, moving finalizeAbort out of runner.js drops vcs-capabilities-table.test.mjs's source-scan below its hardcoded 'at least 2 vcsCapabilities(...) call sites (Publish-PR + finalizeAbort)' assertion, since that test only ever read runner.js.

entries.title: vitest resolves a missing named export to undefined, but node --test hard-fails the whole module
entries.summary: Under Vite's SSR transform a missing named import becomes undefined and the module body still runs, so only tests that call it fail; plain Node ESM raises a link-time SyntaxError and nothing in the file runs.

entries.title: A raw spawnSync ETIMEDOUT message can only come from the outer spawn's own timeout
entries.summary: Verified Node shapes: an execFileSync timeout sets code ETIMEDOUT with a null status and the message 'spawnSync <file> ETIMEDOUT', while a non-zero exit leaves code undefined and produces 'Command failed: ...', so the raw ETIMEDOUT text never arrives via the non-timeout path.

entries.title: Four resolveRepoPath helpers exist in src/tools, but only prime and stats ever had the null-to-cwd shape
entries.summary: kb-session-prime.ts and kb-stats.ts returned string|null and degraded to process.cwd(); kb-export.ts and kb-import.ts have always returned string and thrown, so they were never part of the b4g.7 anchor defect despite the bead naming kb-export as a third instance.

entries.title: Member OS resolution: always via agent.os
entries.summary: The orchestrator and each fleet member can independently run Windows/Mac/Linux -- local members share the orchestrator's own OS, but remote members can be any OS regardless of the orchestrator's. Never assume a target member's shell/OS matches the orchestrator's.

entries.title: apra-fleet-3swo.7 Phase 5 consumer migration end state is fully landed and pinned
entries.summary: readMemberVcsCredentialToken and parseExpiresAtFromProvisionText are completely deleted from fleet-sprint/ (not merely deprecated); buildCredentialReadCommand is deliberately kept dead-in-production/live-in-tests with no deprecation marker; member-provisioning.mjs and coordination.mjs have zero prose-branching (includes/match/toLowerCase) control flow.

entries.title: Setup shell's $$ is unsafe to record for liveness checks under Git Bash on Windows
entries.summary: scripts/sandbox-lock.mjs's acquire CLI previously recorded the Setup shell's self-reported $$, which under Git Bash on Windows is an MSYS-internal pid invisible to defaultDeps.isAlive's native process.kill(pid,0) check -- fixed by having the CLI record its own process.ppid instead, since the CLI process is itself a direct child of the Setup shell and process.ppid always resolves in the native OS pid namespace.

entries.title: dispatch-pin-scanner's moduleSetSource concatenates sources, so line numbers and file labels are only valid for the first module
entries.summary: The pin scanners now build SRC by joining several fleet-sprint modules into one string, so site.line is an offset into the concatenation and every 'runner.js:' label in a pin failure message is hard-coded.

entries.title: Only the settle-shell fleet client was hoisted into sprint state, not every ApraFleet in runner.js
entries.summary: apra-fleet-3swo.6.1 hoisted the settle-shell client into sprint-state.mjs; three other new ApraFleet sites remain in runner.js, and fleetApiForPr is still constructed per PR raise.

entries.title: ROLE_POLICIES doer.secondary and the doer-resume entry are the same object, so anchors look duplicated
entries.summary: role-policies.mjs assigns the doer-resume policy object to doer.secondary, so any sweep iterating ROLE_NAMES and then entry.secondary visits one dispatch twice and reports a false duplicate ladderAnchor.

entries.title: Check a move-only runner.js extraction with a runtime export-surface diff against the base branch
entries.summary: No test in this repo enumerates runner.js's full export surface, so an extraction can silently drop a previously exported symbol; a side-by-side Object.keys diff catches it in seconds.

entries.title: Verbatim-invocation criteria are unsatisfiable for the slow lane
entries.summary: An acceptance criterion demanding verbatim invocation of the regression slow-lane command conflicts with the same bead's ban on running the 8-minute lane, so the reachable evidence is the redirect shape plus a sandboxed stand-in.

entries.title: provisionOutcome's prose fallback in vcs-auth.mjs is live and deliberately pinned
entries.summary: An earlier KB entry calling that fallback dead code and constant-true is wrong: the [FAIL] prose regex still fires even though wrapTool never sets isError, and two tests pin the behaviour.

entries.title: Local vs remote member dispatch paths
entries.summary: Local members share the orchestrator's own machine and credentials, so no SSH or file probe is needed -- check agent.agentType === 'local' and short-circuit. Remote members require actual SSH connectivity and credential probes.

entries.title: Verify a move-only runner.js extraction by normalized line-set diff plus a runtime export-surface diff
entries.summary: Two mechanical checks prove a fleet-sprint move-only extraction without reading the moved code: set-compare the removed lines against the new module after normalizing comment prefixes and the export keyword, then import the old and new runner.js side by side and diff Object.keys.

entries.title: ctx.policies is the seam that makes 'this variance is a policy field, not an engine branch' falsifiable
entries.summary: dispatchRole reads its row through ctx.policies when supplied, so a test can splice ONE field of ONE row and observe the engine behave differently; without it the claim that a variance is data rather than a branch cannot be tested at all.

entries.title: wrapTool already accepts { text, structuredContent }, so adding a structured MCP response needs no tool-registry change
entries.summary: src/services/tool-registry.ts's wrapTool is typed to accept string | { text, structuredContent }, so converting an existing tool from a plain-string return to a structured one requires no edit at the registration site -- only the tool file and its direct consumers.

entries.title: Four distinct git-credential-helper file shapes exist across member OS/shell combinations
entries.summary: The deployed credential helper differs by member OS AND shell: POSIX writes an extensionless $HOME script, windows-powershell writes $env:USERPROFILE\...bat, and windows-gitbash writes a .bat but is invoked through bash -- so any read-side builder needs all three forms plus the PowerShell call operator.

entries.title: A directly launched sprint's deployer self-id is the branch name, not a ledger uuid
entries.summary: runner.js derives the deployer's own reservation id as validated.runId || validated.branch, so a standalone (non-supervisor) launch hands the deployer a branch name rather than a supervisor sprintId.

entries.title: Falsify a fleet-sprint or root-repo test without ever mutating the tracked tree
entries.summary: Copy the module directory to /tmp and revert the single file there, or reconstruct a pure function in a standalone script -- mutating tracked source in place risks a torn read under the concurrent suites and can leave the file corrupted.

entries.title: The mock-sprint and golden suites leak temp files, so 'no artifacts outside the sandbox' cannot be shown by running them
entries.summary: One full mock-sprint pass leaves exactly 10 fleet-sprint-body-*.txt files in the system temp dir and the golden 3-bead suite leaves one sprint-lock entry, independently of any gate that spawns them; npm test already does this twice today.

entries.title: Slicing Integ Test and Re-Review breaks exactly four test baselines, and the Review-C substring pin is the subtle one
entries.summary: The failing set is dispatch-safety-guard's command count, guarded-modules-coverage's not-registered control, beads-transitions-extraction's reopen census and phase-sequence-order's label ownership; golden transcripts and mock-sprint files do NOT break on a true move-only slice.

entries.title: One anchor policy, three branches: verbatim for read tools, hard-fail for kb_export
entries.summary: kb_session_prime and kb_stats pass a supplied repo_path to getKbProviders verbatim so an unreachable remote anchor stays honestly missing; kb_export deliberately keeps throwing instead, because it writes into repo_path -- and it throws before getKbProviders, so it never anchors at the server cwd either.

entries.title: gitRepos is an access list; only a single URL-shaped entry is a usable origin
entries.summary: agent.gitRepos is declared string[] and holds bare "Owner/Repo" access identifiers, not clone URLs. knownRepoRemoteUrl (now in src/services/member-remote-url.ts, re-exported from execute-prompt.ts) returns a URL only when gitRepos has EXACTLY one entry AND that entry is scheme-qualified; anything else yields undefined rather than a guessed URL.

entries.title: hzeb.4.2 usage-limit controller HAS landed on the hzeb branch (older KB entry is stale)
entries.summary: The usage-limit pause/resume controller and dispatchRole onUsageLimit hook are present on fleet-sprint/hzeb-usage-limit-pause as of commit a3cf1fa5; the earlier INFERRED KB claim that hzeb.4.2 code was absent from HEAD is stale.

entries.title: The shared dispatch-role harness stubs out the watchdog, so timeout tests must re-wire the real one
entries.summary: createRecordingCtx's withDispatchWatchdog only records timeoutS/member/label and returns the dispatch promise unchanged, so any test asserting real watchdog timing through dispatchRole must overwrite ctx.withDispatchWatchdog with the implementation from dispatch-failure.mjs.

entries.title: A role's member expression in role-policies.mjs is not role-unique, so it cannot identify a ladder
entries.summary: Three distinct roles share roleMember('planner') and two share roleMember('plan-reviewer'), so any guard that identifies a role's inline dispatch by its member routing expression alone flags other roles' ladders too.

entries.title: The doer needed three engine capabilities no other ladder did, and a spent resume ladder must be terminal
entries.summary: A naive migration of the doer silently changes behaviour in two ways: it re-dispatches a full streak after the escalating resume ladder is spent, and it repeats the D-pulling verifyDoerStreakClosed read.

entries.title: A source-level watchdog explicitness check must resolve secondary-declared roles to their base row
entries.summary: ROLE_NAMES includes doer-resume, which is declared via secondary(doer, 'doer-resume', ...) and has no policy('doer-resume', ...) literal, so a per-role source scan for an explicit watchdog declaration fails unless it follows the secondary back to its base.

entries.title: Measured root npm test split: vitest about 325s over 327 files, then the se suite about 94s
entries.summary: A full root npm test on this tree measured vitest at 324.75s (321 passed, 6 skipped, 327 files) and the apra-fleet-se workspace suite at 94s (3427 pass, 0 fail), with the npm-pack packaging test at 28s -- not the 8-12 minutes an older entry records.

entries.title: install --force cannot stop a launchd/service-manager-relaunched apra-fleet server, no matter how long the SIGKILL grace window is
entries.summary: When the server is registered as a macOS LaunchAgent with KeepAlive on non-successful exit, killing the process directly just makes the service manager relaunch it under a new PID before the installer's liveness poll re-checks, so the installer's poll-and-escalate stop logic always reports failure in this case.

entries.title: runSprintCycle now hosts zero inline phase bodies, and that is mechanically pinned rather than described
entries.summary: After the final slice, runner.js builds no phase() label at all; phase-sequence-order.test.mjs asserts a zero-match shape scan over runner.js with a >=12 count across phases/* as its non-vacuity control.

entries.title: apra-fleet-client's createWorkflowEngine() is dead code -- workflow/ dir does not exist in that package
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-client/src/client/factory.mjs's createWorkflowEngine imports '../workflow/index.mjs' relative to itself, but apra-fleet-client's own src/ tree has no workflow/ directory in this repo state -- any caller must build the client manually (StdioTransport + McpClient + ApraFleet) instead.

entries.title: Slicing a runSprintCycle phase: pass reassigned locals both IN and OUT so the call site needs no conditional
entries.summary: Destructured parameters are assignable in JS, so a moved phase body can keep its `x = ...` statements byte-identical if the caller passes x in and destructures it back out -- which also makes the skip path a no-op without an `if`.

entries.title: The apra-fleet-se workspace suite runs in about 70-90 seconds, not minutes
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-se npm test completes 2618 tests in roughly 70-90s, so it can safely be backgrounded and polled; the 8-12 minute figure belongs to the ROOT vitest suite, not this one.

entries.title: A phases/* module cannot import runner.js helpers -- four pure helpers must be injected through the phase state object
entries.summary: parseBdJson, extractContestedBeadIds, reconcilePendingRejectedNewTasks and stageCommandBodyMemberSide are exported BY runner.js, and resolveSettleShell is runner-module-private, so a phase module must receive them as explicit state rather than importing them.

entries.title: sandbox-deploy allocatePorts rejects adjacent port pairs, so fixed test fixtures must not use consecutive ports
entries.summary: allocatePorts() now rejects any candidate within abs-diff 1 of an already-chosen port (Math.abs(p - port) <= 1, which also subsumes the old exact-duplicate check), because the observed sandbox collision handed back a consecutive fleet/supervisor pair.

entries.title: The pushCode:true dispatch set is four sites (doer + harvester, each with its resume), not two
entries.summary: Both the doer's main dispatch and its max_turns resume, and both the harvester's main dispatch and its resume, pass pushCode:true to withGitSync; every other role dispatch is read-side.

entries.title: phase2-flagged-behaviour-gating.test.mjs binds to commit subjects and a 500-commit window
entries.summary: Its git-level checks locate commits by exact subject line within git log -500 at module load, so they skip wholesale after a squash merge and hard-fail in the partial window once the phase scrolls past depth 500.

entries.title: role-policies-table's deployer ROLE_SOURCE region anchor was wrong, not the deployer's retry.attempts value
entries.summary: The deployer's region start anchor 'const sprintSelfId =' spanned nearly 3000 unrelated lines of runner.js (including the doer's own ladder), causing derivedAttempts()'s RETRY_ONCE_MARKER check to false-positive on the doer's 'Retrying once.' log line.

entries.title: fleet-sprint runner.js's three provision-result emoji regexes are mojibake and never match
entries.summary: runner.js lines 2443, 3171 and 3178 test provision_vcs_auth / provision_llm_auth response text against regexes whose bytes are the UTF-8 encoding of the emoji reinterpreted as Windows-1252, so they can never match a real response and the orchestrator's provision-failure detection is silently dead.

entries.title: Mutate GUARDED_MODULES via a node --import preload to test guard registration without editing files
entries.summary: GUARDED_MODULES is a const binding but a mutable array, so a preload can append to it and exercise the guard tests against a larger registry with the working tree untouched.

entries.title: execFileSync distinguishes a timeout from a non-zero exit by error.code, not error.status
entries.summary: A timed-out execFileSync sets code ETIMEDOUT, signal SIGTERM and status null, while a non-zero exit leaves code undefined and sets status to the exit code with stdout and stderr intact.

entries.title: Verify a fleet-sprint policy-table test by mutating the table, not by reading it
entries.summary: A table-plus-test commit can look thorough while whole fields are unasserted; mutate each field on a clean tree and confirm the test fails, since the file passes either way.

entries.title: guarded-modules-coverage's isAccountedFor() must compare full relative paths, not basenames, to avoid a nested-module collision
entries.summary: Per-guard violation-count baselines correctly compare by basename (guards report violations via path.basename), but the separate 'is every module registered at all' completeness sweep must compare full relative paths, because a nested file (e.g. phases/index.mjs) can share a bare filename with an unrelated top-level registered module (vcs-providers/index.mjs) and would otherwise be silently treated as already covered.

entries.title: Do not dynamically import every runner.js importer -- scripts/dolt-settle-integration.mjs runs main() at module scope
entries.summary: A test that imports each importer of fleet-sprint/runner.js to prove resolution will fire a live MCP connection and real dolt operations from that one file.

entries.title: kb_session_prime must pass an explicit repo_path to getKbProviders verbatim, never through resolveRepoPath
entries.summary: Validating repo_path before handing it to getKbProviders converts a remote member's unreachable path into the fleet server's own cwd, silently staling healthy entries in the shared project KB; the anchor must stay honestly missing.

entries.title: Lockfile drift is invisible to npm test
entries.summary: A PR review that runs only 'npm test' cannot catch package.json/package-lock.json drift (e.g. a dependency override added to package.json without regenerating the lockfile), because npm test runs against whatever node_modules is already populated. Only 'npm ci' -- the reproducible-install path CI actually uses -- reproduces that failure.

entries.title: openSyncBracketCount is a pure aggregate counter; cross-owner bracket overlap is legitimate and relied upon, not a bug
entries.summary: git-sync.mjs's sync-bracket counter has no owner/nesting awareness by design -- runner.js's globalDoerTurn FIFO gate (not the bracket counter) is what keeps code-writing (pushCode:true) dispatches from ever overlapping, and D-push overlap across members is independently safe via the injected dolt push mutex.

entries.title: retry.infraResumeAttempts is a boolean gate, not a count -- a value above 1 is silently ignored
entries.summary: The engine reads infraResumeAttempts only as `> 0`; the resume loop bound comes from retry.resumeAttempts, and the loop re-iterates only on a repeated max_turns exhaustion, never on a repeated infra failure.

entries.title: The fleet-sprint goal-scope reopen guard was inert: 'P2' string compared against a numeric bead.priority
entries.summary: runner.js's goalMax is goalPriorityMax()'s STRING form ('P2') but the reopen guard compared it to a numeric bead.priority, so `3 > 'P2'` was a NaN comparison and the guard never skipped anything at any verdict site until normalizeGoalMax() was added.

entries.title: registerAllTools can be driven by a 4-line fake McpServer, unlocking every handler body for testing
entries.summary: The 'no test loads tool-registry.ts' gap is structural but trivially closable: a fake with tool()/server.sendLoggingMessage() records every registered handler and runs in ~2s.

entries.title: check-generic-boundary.mjs and planner/plan-reviewer NOTES-correction guidance are verifiable by direct string/regex assertion on the shipped .md files
entries.summary: Reviewer/planner-guidance regressions in apra-pm/agents/*.md can be caught with a plain node:test file that reads the file, normalizes whitespace for multi-line phrase matches, and asserts on the correction-marker vocabulary plus the quoting requirement -- no fixture harness needed.

entries.title: role-policies.mjs's secondary() dispatch inherits its main dispatch's member field unless explicitly overridden
entries.summary: secondary(main, role, kind, over) spreads ...main first, so a role's resume/re-ask dispatch shares the SAME member object as its main dispatch for every role in the table today -- any consumer matching dispatches by member-routing expression must de-duplicate across [entry, entry.secondary] or it double-counts one real call site.

entries.title: Node ESM circular imports between runner.js and its extracted fleet-sprint siblings are safe when confined to function bodies
entries.summary: Verified directly (a standalone a.mjs<->b.mjs repro, then live in prompts.mjs/worklists.mjs/abort.mjs) that a module split out of runner.js can import a still-runner.js-resident helper back, and vice versa, without any load-order failure, as long as neither side references the other's binding at top-level module-evaluation time.

entries.title: phase0-seams-facade and vcs-auth-extraction-facade never actually run their nested golden-transcript checks
entries.summary: Both spawn a nested node --test with the inherited NODE_TEST_CONTEXT, so the child no-ops, and both assert nothing beyond execFileSync not throwing.

entries.title: tests/install-force.test.ts afterEach does not actually restore process.platform
entries.summary: Its afterEach redefines process.platform to its own current value, so a platform set by one test leaks into every following test in the file.

entries.title: The default VCS credential label's derivation is unfalsifiable by value, only by source shape
entries.summary: Re-hardcoding vcs-auth.mjs's DEFAULT_VCS_CREDENTIAL_LABEL to the literal 'github' left the entire 2601-test suite green, because DEFAULT_VCS_PROVIDER is itself 'github'; only a source-level assertion on the assignment can gate it.

entries.title: degrade.classes, not degrade.kind, decides what a ladder fabricates -- and the integ runner's omission of 'infra' is the whole INCONCLUSIVE variance
entries.summary: The engine fabricates a value only for the ERROR_CLASSES a row lists in degrade.classes. The integ row lists schema and dispatch but deliberately NOT infra, which is what turns an envelope-less failure into an `inconclusive` record instead of a false passed:false.

entries.title: The APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY regression site is package.json, not run-tests.mjs
entries.summary: scripts/run-tests.mjs has always exported the concurrency var; the inert-scaledTimeout bug was package.json's test script bypassing run-tests.mjs, so a guard that spawns run-tests.mjs directly cannot catch it.

entries.title: A sprint's own reservation is always in GET /api/sprints while it deploys
entries.summary: The supervisor reservation ledger always contains the deploying sprint's own entry, so any 'non-empty sprints array => stop' deploy gate blocks every sprint from deploying its own work; identity must be compared exactly on sprintId.

entries.title: pushBeadsAfter's real gap vs doltPushAfter was the non-throwing degrade contract, not retry/lease-renewal (those already lived inside doltPushAfter itself)
entries.summary: doltPushAfter() already contains retry (via runDoltStep's maxTransientRetries), mutex lease renewal, and settle-callback support regardless of caller; DoltSync.syncAfter()'s real value-add over a bare doltPushAfter() call is wrapping it in runDegradable(), which catches an unresolved failure and returns a structured {degraded:true} outcome instead of always throwing.

entries.title: cli.mjs self-invoke must be gated on NODE_TEST_CONTEXT so the phase4 move-only probe does not fire main()
entries.summary: bin/cli.mjs's isMainModule() self-invokes main() whenever process.argv[1] resolves to this module. The Phase-4 move-only probe runs a copy of cli.mjs under `node --test`, which leaves argv[1] pointing at the copy, so main() ran and exited 1 on missing required flags, classifying the file UNEXPLAINED and failing the gate. Gating the self-invoke on process.env.NODE_TEST_CONTEXT fixes it without affecting production launch or the workflow import trampoline.

entries.title: resolveProjectSlug prefers an explicit git remote URL over shelling git against repo_path
entries.summary: resolveProjectSlug(cwd, remoteUrl) slugifies remoteUrl directly when supplied and only falls back to `git remote get-url origin` against cwd, then the repo dirname, then 'default', when no URL is given -- letting remote members (whose repo_path is unreachable from the fleet server host) resolve to the same slug as a local clone.

entries.title: The harness vcs_credential_exec simulator records into commandLog but never into the workflow activityLog
entries.summary: A command dispatched through defaultMockCallTool's vcs_credential_exec branch reaches mockFleetApi.executeCommand directly, so it appears in commandLog/commandLogDetailed but emits no activity:start event and is invisible to activityLog-based assertions.

entries.title: phase1-leaf-facade-completeness.test.mjs flakes under full npm test concurrency due to nested node --test spawn contention
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-se's phase1-leaf-facade-completeness.test.mjs subtest '(4) every mock-sprint test file passes' spawns its own nested `node --test --test-concurrency=8` over 62 mock-sprint-*.test.mjs files; running this while the OUTER `npm test` suite is also at --test-concurrency=8 causes resource contention that intermittently fails it, even though the same test passes 100% reliably in isolation.

entries.title: apra-fleet-se's spawner.test.mjs orphan-survival/SIGKILL tests flake only under full node --test concurrency
entries.summary: test/spawner.test.mjs's real detached-child-process tests (orphan survival, SIGKILL cleanup) failed twice in one full `npm test` run (test-concurrency=8, ~700+ files) with 'sanity check: our own cleanup kill worked' and a cascading subtest failure, but passed 30/30 in isolation and again 0/0-fail on a second full-suite run -- a resource-contention flake tied to concurrent process spawning under load, not a functional regression.

entries.title: SqliteProvider freshness verdicts must be suppressed, not re-hashed, when the repo anchor is unreachable
entries.summary: A repo_path that does not exist on this host (the remote-member case) must never fall back to process.cwd() as the freshness anchor, and must not be re-hashed against it either -- both checkFreshness and freshnessSweep now short-circuit to a no-op verdict via a shared anchorIsMissing() check instead.

entries.title: Falsify a phases/* slice by set-diffing the diff's removed lines against the new modules
entries.summary: Normalizing leading whitespace and sorting lets `comm` prove a move-only extraction dropped nothing and added nothing but scaffolding, which reading a 700-line diff by eye cannot establish.

entries.title: execute_prompt now wires detectUsageLimit into the dispatch path (usage_limit relay landed)
entries.summary: As of commit ad1146ac on hzeb-onto-refactor, execute_prompt calls provider.detectUsageLimit after every parseResponse and relays reason:'usage_limit'; earlier 'detection is inert / relay does not exist' KB entries are stale.

entries.title: A fallback message sharing the assertion's alternate keyword makes a test vacuous
entries.summary: checkDoltRemoteAbsent's bd-unavailable fallback messages all contain the word "unavailable", so the old combined assertion /Dolt-level remotes|unavailable/ was satisfied on any machine without bd without ever reaching the parser under test. Merged main closes this by probing bd --version first and asserting the two cases separately. The reusable trap: never OR an assertion's success keyword with its own fallback keyword.

entries.title: An unguarded cat of a shell marker file degrades to a wrong diagnosis, not a loud failure
entries.summary: regression-test-playbook.md's poll loop computed UPTIME_DEADLINE=$(( SUPERVISOR_STARTED_AT + 280 )) from an uncheck-ed cat; a missing marker made it evaluate to a bare 280, exiting 1 with the dolt-orphan-sweep tick message and sending operators after a nonexistent timing bug.

entries.title: bdListScoped gives fresh STATUS but never fresh SCOPE -- scope always comes from the cached snapshot
entries.summary: A filtered bdListScoped() call issues a real bd list, but intersects it with scopeIds derived from the possibly-stale allBeadsSnapshot, so a bead CREATED behind the command() seam stays invisible until the snapshot drops even on a 'fresh' read.

entries.title: In Git Bash, a background job's $! is an MSYS pid that never equals the process's own process.pid
entries.summary: Under MSYS/MinGW bash on Windows, $! returns the MSYS-internal pid while a spawned native Node process reports a different native Windows pid via process.pid, so any script that proves identity by comparing $! against a pid the process reports about itself can never match.

entries.title: Two ladder anchors match two call sites each because resume prompts re-embed their main prompt variable
entries.summary: An exactly-one assertion on role policy ladder anchors cannot hold: integ-test-runner and regression-test-runner resume prompts concatenate their own main prompt variable, so those two main anchors legitimately match two agent() sites.

entries.title: The sync-bracket guarantee is now mechanically scanned by a fifth guard, not just a convention
entries.summary: As of e9e585c4 a fifth guard scans every guarded module for bare sync primitives, superseding the earlier claim that nothing enforced the bracket rule.

entries.title: normalizeMsysPathForPlatform is the required seam before path.resolve on any env-sourced path
entries.summary: Node's path.resolve does not understand MSYS /c/... paths and on win32 prefixes them with the current drive, so any filesystem path arriving from a Git Bash environment variable must go through normalizeMsysPathForPlatform first.

entries.title: StdioTransport.stop() is synchronous -- awaiting it with .catch() throws a TypeError
entries.summary: apra-fleet-client's StdioTransport.stop() returns undefined, so the common teardown idiom `await stop().catch(() => {})` throws TypeError inside a finally block and skips the cleanup after it.

entries.title: DEGRADE_STEPS is separate from POST_RESULT_STEPS because the reviewer's round session must be dropped on failure and kept on success
entries.summary: role-policies.mjs has three step vocabularies, and the split is load-bearing rather than tidy: a step in the wrong list gets the per-round reviewer's session handling exactly backwards.

entries.title: A nested node --test child silently no-ops unless NODE_TEST_CONTEXT is stripped from its env
entries.summary: node --test sets NODE_TEST_CONTEXT on its own process; a child spawned with it still present returns empty stdout and exit 0 without running anything, so any nested-suite gate must delete it and then assert a non-zero '# pass' count.

entries.title: dispatchRole resolves a dispatch's options INSIDE the git-sync bracket, and opts.prepare is why
entries.summary: The engine builds agent() options inside invoke(), i.e. inside withGitSync, because an in-bracket pre-dispatch step can change what the dispatch should say -- the doer's claim narrows its streak after the bracket's D-pull, and the prompt, label and per-bead tier all follow.

entries.title: Phase 2 commit taxonomy: git-sync.mjs's extraction is not a move-only commit
entries.summary: Of this phase's extraction commits only coordination/kb, beads-scope and beads-transitions are move-only; the git-sync.mjs extraction closed two pause-guard holes by construction, so later sync-layer behaviour changes legitimately edit the file it created.

entries.title: .fleet/ mixes a tracked deliverable (kb-canonical.json) with per-round scratch (planner-output.json)
entries.summary: Before adding a .gitignore rule under .fleet/, check git ls-files first -- .fleet/kb-canonical.json is a tracked, checked-in KB export deliverable, so a blanket '.fleet/' ignore rule would silently shadow it exactly the way this repo's own sprint-logs/ note warns against for directory-level ignore rules.

entries.title: Sandbox module imports in fleet-sprint tests must use pathToFileURL().href, not a raw absolute path
entries.summary: A raw absolute path handed to dynamic import() fails on Windows (parsed as scheme 'c:') and also fails on POSIX whenever the tmpdir path contains a space or '#'.

entries.title: KB knowledge reaches a dispatch by one of three paths, and a resume dispatch of a self-injecting role gets none
entries.summary: The agent() wrapper injects the knowledge block only for an agentType outside KB_SELF_INJECTING_ROLES; doer/reviewer get it from their prompt builders; a dispatch with no agentType, and every resume prompt of a self-injecting role, receives no block at all.

entries.title: The repo's commit hook ASCII check silently no-ops on macOS because it uses grep -P
entries.summary: A git commit of N changed files prints N 'grep: invalid option -- P' lines on macOS BSD grep; the commit succeeds and the hook's non-ASCII check never actually runs.

entries.title: A fleet-sprint sandbox copy under os.tmpdir needs a node_modules symlink, and rmSync will not follow it
entries.summary: Copying fleet-sprint/ outside the repo breaks bare-specifier resolution for @apralabs workspace packages, so the sandbox must symlink the hoisted node_modules back in; fs.rmSync recursive cleanup unlinks that symlink without recursing into the real directory.

entries.title: sprintMutexId pins the member-reservation key, not the engine run-state runId
entries.summary: cli.mjs reserves members with sprintId: branchName always, while effectiveRunId (run-id or branchName) keys only run-state files -- the two diverge under a supervisor launch.

entries.title: regression-test-playbook.md's Setup/Reset/Teardown headings appear as backticked prose mentions elsewhere in the file, so naive string.split('## Setup') is unsafe
entries.summary: Any script or test that wants to isolate the Setup/Reset/Teardown sections of regression-test-playbook.md by splitting on the heading text must anchor to a whole line (e.g. /^## Setup$/m), not do a plain substring split -- the file's own intro and cross-reference prose repeatedly mentions `## Setup`, `## Reset`, `## Teardown` inside backticks well before the real headings, and a plain .split('## Setup')[1] picks up that prose fragment instead of the actual section body.

entries.title: The sprint run id reaches runner.js only via buildRunnerArgs' run_id key
entries.summary: spawner --run-id -> cli.mjs effectiveRunId existed but was dropped at buildRunnerArgs, so runner.js had no reservation identity; run_id must be added to both buildRunnerArgs and runner.js KNOWN_ARG_KEYS/validateArgs.

entries.title: retry.authSelfHealShortCircuits is inert at final-review's shipped attempts=2 and can only be observed by splicing attempts=3
entries.summary: The healed retry consumes attempt one, so at a two-attempt budget the short-circuit and the generic retry coincide; a mutation test must raise attempts on BOTH arms and vary only the flag, otherwise the field reads identically either way and looks unfalsifiable.

entries.title: A nested extraPaths fixture cannot pin the guard-baseline basename bug -- only a nested GUARDED_MODULES entry can
entries.summary: Comparing a guard's files output against GUARDED_MODULES versus guardedModuleBasenames() gives identical results while every registered entry is flat, so a regression test that nests only a caller-supplied fixture is vacuous.

entries.title: ClaudeProvider.detectUsageLimit treats a bare 429 as a usage limit without the limit-message
entries.summary: After hzeb.1.4.1, a 429 apiErrorStatus is classified as a usage limit on its own; the 'hit your <...> limit' message is only required for the non-429 terminalReason==='api_error' path.

entries.title: resolveNestedSuiteTimeoutMs is directly callable, so its env override and fallback branches need no module re-init to test
entries.summary: The phase1 budget resolver is a pure module-scope function of process.env; asserting only the handler's budgetSource wording leaves the default, override and unparseable branches untested.

entries.title: Three source-pinning tests read withGitSync's body out of runner.js, not just the two bracket-count guards
entries.summary: Beyond dispatch-safety-guard/dispatch-sync-bracket-coverage, moving withGitSync out of runner.js breaks vcs-auth-preflight.test.mjs's needsVcsAuth default regex, mock-sprint-retry-resume-remote-tip.test.mjs's skipPreDispatchSync ordering guard, and runner-clean-state-pause-guard.test.mjs's new Function source slice.

entries.title: mock-sprint network guard misses absolute-path curl invocations
entries.summary: isNetworkShapedCommand() matches only a bare curl/wget token, so an absolute-path invocation like /usr/bin/curl reaches the real runCmd() fallback and the host network.

entries.title: The ctx.steps hook bodies are the one part of a migrated ladder no dispatch-pin test executes
entries.summary: dispatch-role-harness.mjs supplies recording stubs for ctx.steps, so runner.js's own step implementations are proved to be INVOKED but never proved to be CORRECT by the pin tests.

entries.title: vi.mock('node:child_process') makes WindowsServiceManager.isInstalled() return true in tests
entries.summary: Any install.ts code path gated on ServiceManager.isInstalled() takes the service branch under win32 in tests/install-force.test.ts, because the auto-mocked execFileSync never throws.

entries.title: runner.js keeps a withGitSync alias so the two bracket source-guards survive the git-sync.mjs extraction
entries.summary: dispatch-sync-bracket-coverage and git-sync-brackets both scan runner.js with a lookbehind regex that skips gitSync.withGitSync(, so the local alias at runner.js:4075 is load-bearing, not cosmetic.

entries.title: The dispatchRole engine must spell agent( and ctx.withGitSync( literally or the guards lose it
entries.summary: dispatch-role.mjs destructures agent from ctx so the guards' call-site regexes still match its one dispatch, while the bracket and watchdog stay ctx-qualified and are asserted by regex instead.

entries.title: dolt-orphan-sweep owner scoping is opt-in via FLEET_SE_SWEEP_OWNER_DATA_DIR, and must stay opt-in
entries.summary: buildSweepCommand() accepts an owner data-dir prefix that both shell families enforce, wired by bin/serve.mjs from FLEET_SE_SWEEP_OWNER_DATA_DIR; it cannot be derived from FLEET_SE_DATA_DIR because the ephemeral --data-dir belongs to the member, not the supervisor.
